notes_body: Kinematics page Fig 5.1: FAR_DIR = (far_L - far_R) / 2 of the per-trial sideways jaw displacement while the jaw is open (+ = toward the target far spout; drift common to both sides cancels); cam4 LP v36 (cleaning v35), measured jaw frames only; 107 sessions, 51,355 trials of the camera working period.

Acutely the jaw stops steering toward the far target in every animal: pooled -11.7 px [-13.7, -9.2]; per-animal epoch means pre -> acute PS92 13.0 -> 0.7, PS93 8.2 -> 0.4, PS94 12.0 -> -0.8, PS95 15.3 -> 1.4 px. Subacute -5.9 [-9.1, -3.0]. Chronic -4.1 [-6.7, -1.3]: the pooled interval excludes 0, but the deficit is carried by two animals (PS92 5.5 vs 13.0 pre, PS93 2.7 vs 8.2; PS94 11.5 vs 12.0, PS95 12.3 vs 15.3), so a lasting deficit is not established under the 3-of-4 rule.

3-D agrees animal by animal (kinematics page Fig 7.5 bottom row, jaw FAR_DIR, mm): acute -0.26 / -0.21 / -0.41 / -0.32 (PS92-95), pooled -0.30 [-0.38, -0.23]; subacute -0.15 [-0.21, -0.08]; chronic -0.09 [-0.15, -0.02], carried by PS92 / PS93 (-0.14 / -0.15 vs -0.02 / -0.03).

Figure rules (Priya 11-03): no lines across epochs; per-animal mean +- SEM (filled, shape = animal, color = epoch) with its sessions as faded open markers. notes_body: Recovery analysis 1 (Priya 10-30; Bollu T, Ito BS, Whitehead SC, Kardon B, Redd J, Liu MH, Goldberg JH (2021) Cortex-dependent corrections as the tongue reaches for and misses targets. Nature 594:82-87: corrective submovements are ALM-dependent). 250 Hz 3-D tongue, far-contralesional spout, cued post-cue licks (all orders and outcomes) of camera-working-period trials, PS92-95, August pre. Launch angle = direction of the first 12 ms of protrusion; endpoint = angle at the extension peak; both relative to the animal's pre-stroke hits. Corrective submovement (CSM) = an extra speed peak above a noise-calibrated threshold (50 mm/s; noise alone 5.0 % of pre cued licks vs 16.1 % real). Pre-stroke the Bollu signatures hold: CSMs 0.28-0.33 at the far side spouts vs 0.04-0.07 at the close spouts.

After the stroke the launch is aimed ipsilesionally: -25.7 deg acute [-34.3, -17.0], -7.0 subacute [-12.7, -2.6] (4 / 4 each, Holm p .002), recovering to -3.2 chronic (n.s.). The endpoint follows the launch; the within-lick correction does not change in any epoch (-0.3 / -1.3 / -0.4 deg, n.s.), and the CSM share FALLS (-0.13 / -0.15 / -0.14; 4 / 4, 4 / 4, 3 / 4; chronic misses Holm, p_holm .068).

Reading: the brain fixes the launch command itself rather than adding feedback corrections. In-flight correction is IMPAIRED early (toward-target correction -5.1 deg acutely, 4 / 4; missed later licks lose their pre-stroke re-aim, -8.0 deg acutely, 4 / 4; within-lick gain dips subacutely, -0.14, 4 / 4) and recovers chronically, but never exceeds pre, so it is not the route to recovery.

Stats: pooled session level with 95 % nested bootstrap CI; top-band * = CI excludes 0 AND >= 3 / 4 animals same sign; ** = also Holm over the 9 primary tests. Caveats: 'launch' starts at the first tracked frame (~1.5 mm out), so it includes where the tongue emerges; 250 Hz resolves only submovements >= ~20 ms. Script scripts/within_lick_correction.py; prereg + outcome docs/status/WITHIN_LICK_CORRECTION_PREREG_20261030.md. PROVISIONAL, n = 4.
